summary.intent: Drive the CipherBox v2 write-plane frontier (issues #861-#864 plus follow-on #876/#879/#880 dependency wiring) from implementation through ship (verify, security/crypto review, simplify, local gates, CodeRabbit, PR, merge) using parallel worktree agents and ship workers, while also fixing a recurring gap where triage-filed issues weren't getting native dependency edges set.
summary.outcome: #861 and #863 merged (PR #874, #875); #862 and #864 (PR #877, #878) sequenced through review with rebases/conflict handled; native GitHub dependency edges added for #876/#879/#880; three stale tracker checkboxes fixed; and the /ship command file was patched to fix issue-edge-setting and two other instruction gaps that had caused failures this session (a commit was in progress on a branch at transcript end).

repo: Worktree agents have no node_modules, so husky/lint-staged commit hooks always fail there — they commit with --no-verify and rely on CI lint as the backstop; markdown formatting must be re-verified from the main checkout.
cargo fmt must always be run as `cargo fmt --all`, never `-p`, per repo convention enforced across all agents.
KAT vectors/manifests must be regenerated via `kat_gen` examples, never hand-edited; freshness is checked in CI via `git diff --exit-code` after regeneration.

This repo has been previously bitten by branches that merge cleanly (textually) but break the combined workspace compile — always do a real compiled test-merge, not just a git merge simulation, before shipping stacked branches.

GitHub PR ancestry checks (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) report NOT MERGED after a squash-merge even though the PR is merged — verify via `gh pr view`/GitHub state, not local ancestry, before deleting branches.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file`.
CodeRabbit reviews run ~1/hour org-wide and only trigger on PR-ready (not draft) — review slot availability, not diff size, is the throughput bottleneck for shipping multiple PRs.

This repo uses GitHub's native issue dependency edges (blocked_by/blocking) as the actual tracking mechanism, distinct from prose 'Depends on #N' — issues without native edges are invisible to tracking automation. Convention shown in tracker as `#868 <- 867,862`.
Sub-issue/parent GitHub mechanism (#813 has 21 sub-issues) is used for wayfinder/design questions, not for build-slice tracking, which stays prose-only ('Part of #655') plus native blocked_by edges.

Casting a hand-assembled object `as unknown as EngineWasm` in test harness code (packages/client/test/browser/engine.worker.ts) erases compile-time member checks, letting a new required field pass typecheck and only fail at runtime inside the worker — the Client Browser Suite is the only gate that catches this class of bug.

Closed GitHub issues (#819, #824, #832, #820) are used as 'wayfinder'/design-resolution issues in this repo, not open trackers — filing follow-up work against them orphans it; file against an open umbrella (#655) or open consuming slice instead.

code.finding: New 15th frozen KDF edge settings_ipns_keypair derives from login secret alone (no index/epoch), making the settings IPNS name unrotatable by construction — accepted as deliberate per issue #861/design record #825/#813.

assemble() previously didn't validate leaf-CID well-formedness while decode_root() hard-rejected malformed CIDs — an asymmetry violating the repo's encode/decode fail-closed rule (AGENTS.md rule-8); fixed with a release-active Err(MalformedLeafCid) guard in issue #862's slice.

OP_RECORD_V is bound into HPKE AAD but not carried in the clear header; a future version bump would make all queued op records fail auth and get dead-lettered/deleted as Undecodable, silently destroying users' offline queues — flagged as needing a decision before #865 builds on this shape, later folded into #864's scope per user direction.

Hand-assembled EngineWasm object cast via `as unknown as EngineWasm` bypassed compile-time member checking, masking a runtime failure when PendingClass was added; fixed by making the test worker match production's dynamic namespace import.

workflow: Background ship workers must be instructed to wait inline via chained foreground sleeps for slow async events (e.g. ~35min CodeRabbit review cooldown) rather than ending their turn to 'stand by' — an agent that stops has no mechanism to resume itself, silently stalling the pipeline ('lost-wake' failure mode).

Before shipping stacked/dependent branches, simulate the full sequential merge and build the combined tree (cargo check + test), not just pairwise git merge checks — semantic interactions between compile-clean branches can still break behaviorally.

When an agent's self-review (internal simplify/security/crypto pass before commit) is offered as evidence, it does not substitute for the mandated /simplify, /security-review, /crypto-privacy-review gates being run against the actual PR diff by the ship worker.
Draft PRs can be deliberately held (not marked ready) to control which PR claims a scarce review-bot time slot, sequencing multiple in-flight PRs competing for the same CodeRabbit review capacity.

When a subagent's prediction is wrong (e.g. predicted KAT-manifest conflict between #861/#862 that didn't materialize because #862 used a separate directory), state that explicitly and correct the record rather than let it stand.

friction: Ship worker for #863 ended its turn 'standing by' for a ~35-minute CodeRabbit review cooldown instead of waiting inline, requiring a manual restart with corrected instructions (lost-wake failure).
First workspace test run for #861 was piped through `tail -40`, truncating output and making verification unreliable; had to re-run capturing full output.

Issue #876 (filed during #862's ship) was created with prose-only 'Depends on' text and zero native GitHub dependency edges, making it invisible to tracker automation — same gap recurred for #879 and #880.
Tracker #655 had three stale unchecked checkboxes (#633, #640, #644) for issues that were actually already closed, discovered only via a full audit.

#864's implementation surfaced a genuine spec-tension decision (clear op-record version vs settled #832 §3 three-part format) that required user adjudication rather than being resolvable unilaterally by the agent.
